title: A worker's brief names the paths always in scope, so a content worker adds a source row whose count regenerates the _coverage files
goal: a worker's brief names the paths every item may change (bl_base.always_in_scope: the item files and the generated _coverage.csv and _coverage.md), so a content worker that finds an official page adds the source row whose count regenerates those files and does not drop it as outside its touches

clauses.clause: a worker's brief names the paths every item may change (bl_base.always_in_scope: the item files and the generated _coverage.csv and _coverage.md), so a content worker that finds an official page adds the source row whose count regenerates those files and does not drop it as outside its touches

gates.question: Where does the worker's brief name the paths always in scope: as one line of its fixed rules, or as a section of its own?
options: one line of the fixed rules
gates.recommendation: one line of the fixed rules
gates.answer: one line of the fixed rules

notes: SP-5x5ut5ko retrospective: two workers (ST-owblgazg, ST-tjaxw22f) found an official page that states a fact, added its source row, then dropped it because the topic's source count regenerates kb/public/_coverage.csv and _coverage.md, outside their touches; the fact went in as an UNK lead or a reword. Premise run 2026-10-12 does not reproduce as filed: bl_base.in_scope('kb/public/_coverage.csv', []) and the .md are True (always_in_scope holds kb/*/_coverage.csv and .md in the defaults and in backlog.json), so done and check already count them in scope. What is left: no line of the worker's brief (bl_dispatch.worker_rules, the item JSON) names the always-in-scope paths, so a worker reads its touches alone. Reshaped from a done/plan change to that brief line. Planned at the 2026-10-12 draft triage (sprint 16 of 19, "Land snags: gate answers committed by the tool, link touches, stale-touch reads, generated coverage files and the undelivered warning"): it fixes a failure that recurred in recent sprints and blocks the EP-gzr4mmkm fitness test that a content sprint lands on headless Sonnet workers with no operator step beyond its gates.
